audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for secret anointing, coup dynamics, watchtower reports, Joram and Ahaziah killings, Naboth-land oracle, Jezebel's presentation and taunt, eunuch participation, trampling, body desecration, and prophetic fulfillment rhetoric.

modern.text: When Jehu went out to the servants of his master, they asked, “Is everything all right? Why did this madman come to you?” “You know his kind and their babble,” he replied.

modern.text: “That is a lie!” they said. “Tell us now!” So Jehu answered, “He talked to me about this and that, and he said, ‘This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.’”

modern.text: but King Joram had returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds he had suffered at the hands of the Arameans in the battle against Hazael their king.) So Jehu said, “If you commanders wish to make me king, then do not let anyone escape from the city to go and tell it in Jezreel.”

familiar.text: And there stood a watchman on the tower in Jezreel, and he spied the company of Jehu as he came, and said, I see a company. And Joram said, Take an horseman, and send to meet them, and let him say, Is it peace?

modern.text: Now the watchman standing on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu’s troops approaching, and he called out, “I see a company of troops!” “Choose a rider,” Joram commanded. “Send him out to meet them and ask, ‘Have you come in peace?’”

verses.restored: The horseman went to meet him and said, Thus says king: Is there peace? Jehu said, What is there to you and peace? Turn behind me. Watchman reported, Messenger reached them and does not return.

familiar.text: So there went one on horseback to meet him, and said, Thus saith the king, Is it peace? And Jehu said, What hast thou to do with peace? turn thee behind me. And the watchman told, saying, The messenger came to them, but he cometh not again.

modern.text: So a horseman rode off to meet Jehu and said, “This is what the king asks: ‘Have you come in peace?’” “What do you know about peace?” Jehu replied. “Fall in behind me.” And the watchman reported, “The messenger reached them, but he is not coming back.”

modern.text: So the king sent out a second horseman, who went to them and said, “This is what the king asks: ‘Have you come in peace?’” “What do you know about peace?” Jehu replied. “Fall in behind me.”

translation_notes: Jehu's anointing is secret, hurried, and immediately becomes a military coup. Prophetic commissioning does not remove accountability for methods, targets, or civilian consequences.
The command to destroy Ahab's entire house repeats dynastic-extermination rhetoric and must never justify family killing, inherited guilt, or political purges.
Calling the prophetic messenger a 'madman' reflects contempt toward ecstatic or unusual behavior; it must not be weaponized against mentally ill or neurodivergent people.
Joram is killed while recovering from battle wounds, and Ahaziah is pursued and killed while visiting him. Coup success is not due process.
Naboth's murdered family is invoked as the moral grievance behind Joram's death, but restorative justice cannot be achieved through another unlawful killing.
Jezebel's cosmetics and arranged hair may signal royal dignity, defiance, seduction, or death preparation. They must not support misogynistic readings that blame appearance, sexuality, or femininity.
Jezebel is thrown from a window, trampled, eaten by dogs, and denied burial. This is body desecration and gendered humiliation, not a spiritually satisfying ending.
The eunuchs' role may reflect palace coercion, survival, or alliance with Jehu; the text does not grant access to their motives.
Prophetic-fulfillment language reports the narrator's theology but does not make corpse abuse, misogyny, or coup violence ethically normative.
safety_note: Do not use 2 Kings 9 to justify coups, summary execution, family extermination, misogyny toward Jezebel, mental-health slurs, corpse desecration, or the claim that prophetic authorization removes legal and moral accountability. Keep Naboth's injustice visible without turning vengeance into justice.
